371042.title: Embedding conjecture for three-dimensional symmetric designs from regular Hadamard matrices

The current Conjecture 5.3 has different parameters (v^6(v^6-1)/2 etc.) and the source says it follows from Theorem 4.11(ii) once a regular Hadamard H of order v^2 embeds in a regular Hadamard matrix of order v^4. Observation (not credited): H tensor (h_11 H) is regular of order v^4 and its top-left block equals H, so the embedding is immediate and the Theorem 4.14 argument with regular K and Theorem 4.11(ii) appears to give Conjecture 5.3 in one paragraph. This is a source-ingredient bridge plus a classical Kronecker fact: zero credit under the 369221/374488 precedent. Not formalized.

371239.title: The Gowers norm additive uncertainty conjecture
371239.review_depth: source v1 Section 5 (Definition 5.1, Conjecture 5.2) read in full; exact computations; prior-art abstract arXiv:2609.06531 read
371239.investigation: This lane independently found the same counterexample: f = delta_0 - delta_1 on Z_3 gives |E| = 2, Sigma = {1,2}, Q_k(Sigma) = 2 + 2k, so |E|^{k+1} Q_k < 3^{k+1} for every k >= 6 (exact: 1792/2187 at k = 6). Exact prime-group search: in Z_3, Z_5, Z_7 and Z_11 the conjecture holds for k <= 5 and fails first at k = 6 (Z_3), 7 (Z_5) and 8 (Z_11), with none for Z_7 up to k = 7. A floating diagnostic over Z_4, Z_6 and Z_3^2 found no failure for k <= 5. BUT Vranesko, arXiv:2609.06531 (2026-09-06), already publishes exactly this two-point Z_3 counterexample for every k >= 6. EXCLUDED as prior art.

371321.title: Generalized asymmetric three-colour Ramsey conjecture
371321.investigation: Three-colour asymmetric Folkman-type existence. The l = 2 case reduces to the source two-colour theorem (R(k)-1 >= k+1). For l >= 3 it needs a genuinely three-colour arrowing G -> (K_{k+1}, K_{k-1}, K_l). Sviridenkov (2026) extends the source to hypergraphs and to many colours on the non-arrowing side, but keeps a two-colour target side (K_s, K_{t_l - 1}), which does not imply the conjecture: merging colours yields only a K_{l-1} in the merged class. Container/probabilistic machinery; complete graphs settle only sporadic small cases (for example k = l = 3 via R(4,3) = 9 < R(3,3,3) = 17). Parked.

371344.title: Prime-diagonal rank conjecture for graphical Hermite simplices
371344.review_depth: source v2 (arXiv:2511.03822, 2026-06-22) Definition 2.2, Corollary 4.10, Conjecture 4.11 read
371344.investigation: Two-line proof (not credited as routine): for an increasing DAG, A = pI + B is upper triangular with det A = p^n, so every invariant factor divides p^n and is a power of p. Reducing the Smith normal form mod p, the number of invariant factors not divisible by p equals rank_{F_p}(A mod p) = rank_{F_p}(B) = r. Hence alpha_1 = ... = alpha_r = 1 and alpha_{r+1} > 1 (r <= n-1 since B is nilpotent). This is a one-paragraph bridge from the definitions and standard SNF facts: zero credit. The ELA published version was not read (journal page seen in search only).

371394.title: EISPN conjectures for Cartesian products of paths
371394.review_depth: source arXiv:2511.07248 v1 definitions, Section 7 (EIS-efficiency) and Conjecture 2 read
371394.investigation: EISPN(G) <= n(G), because each vertex is a private neighbour of at most one kind. The source itself cites Hedetniemi et al. [13] (Utilitas Math. 124 (2025)): for 3 <= m <= 5, every grid G_{n,m} is EIS-efficient (EISPN = n(G)) except G_{3,3}, G_{5,3}, G_{3,5} and G_{9,5}. P_3 box P_{2k} (even side) and P_4 box P_m avoid all the exceptions, so EISPN equals 6k and 4m. The conjecture therefore follows from a result printed in the source: zero credit. [13] was not read directly (source paraphrase only).

371606.title: Irreducibility of extremal synchronizing automata
371606.review_depth: source v2 and Semigroup Forum version (2026-08-05) Conjecture 1.1 and Section 5 read
371606.investigation: Extremal implies C-irreducible. Exhaustive check: all automata with n = 3 states and alphabets of at most 3 non-identity letters (54 extremal, none reducible), and all binary automata with n = 4 (48 extremal, none reducible), using the Burnside dimension test mod two primes. A counterexample would be a new extremal (Cerny-length) automaton, which is unlikely given the known catalogues. Parked.

371607.title: Rank-two word conjecture for irreducible automata
371607.review_depth: source v2 and published Semigroup Forum version (2026-08-05): Definition 2.1, synchronized representation, Section 4 assumptions, Conjecture 5.2 read; exact certificates
371607.investigation: Conjecture 5.2 (irreducible implies a word of rank 2) is false. (a) Trivial circular example: Q = {0,1,2}, letters a = (0 1 2), b = (0 1), c = constant 0. It is synchronizing, image sizes are {3, 1} only, and it is C-irreducible because the sum-zero module of S_3 is irreducible (certificate: 4 word matrices spanning M_2(Q)). The same works for S_n plus a constant letter for every n >= 3. (b) Binary example found by exhaustive search: Q = {0,...,4}, a = (0 1 2 3)(4), b = [0,2,0,4,0]. Reachable images have sizes {5, 3, 1} (8 image sets), the shortest reset word is bb, and 16 word matrices (up to length 5) are linearly independent over Q; every elementary matrix is an explicit Q-combination of them (exact certificate). Exhaustive coverage: all binary automata with n = 4 (none); n = 5 with a permutation letter (16 found); circular binary automata (a = n-cycle) for n = 4..7: none. SIGNIFICANCE RISK: example (a) is the standard "synchronizing group plus constant map" object, so root may judge the refutation trivial (373480 precedent). Prior art: no published counterexample found; Lean Pool (HEAD 01db1d70, full tree), cached Omega/OpenAI lists and 3 GitHub searches gave no hits. See CANDIDATE.md.

371619.title: Exact star-colored Turán bound conjecture
371619.review_depth: source arXiv:2511.17000 v1 Theorem 1.5 with proof, Theorem 3.1, definitions, Conjecture 7.1 read; literature search
371619.investigation: Exact minimum-hitting-set search over (edge, colour) items. The conjecture holds (no configuration exceeds s t(n, r-1)) for (r,s,n) = (4,3,4), (4,3,5), (4,4,5), (4,3,6) and (5,4,5). (4,3,7) and (5,4,6) exceeded the 100 s cap. The r = 3 case is the cited Theorem 3.1. Construction checks (r-2 complete graphs; K_n plus two triangle-free graphs) fall short of the bound. An exact proof for all n would need a stability argument beyond Theorem 1.5 (which loses sn). Parked.
